pull.title: KAFKA-20684 [5/N]: Migrate Streams to RebalanceListener
pull.body:
StreamsRebalanceListener implements RebalanceListener and StreamThread registers it via setRebalanceListener. RegexSourceIntegrationTest now intercepts by overriding setRebalanceListener, since that is what StreamThread calls. StreamThreadTest's subscribe verifications are split so they keep valid assertions.

Reviewers: Andrew Schofield <aschofield@confluent.io>, Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body: Thanks for the PR. The integration with Kafka Streams is interesting because the actual consumer is part of the TaskManager, so the reference provided on the rebalance callbacks is never used. I wonder whether the tests should in some way assert that.

review_comments.body: Looking at how Kafka Streams plumbs in the rebalance listener, it seems to me that the supplied RebalanceConsumer is not actually used by the TaskManager. I wonder if actually the test should mock a RebalanceConsumer and assert that its methods are never called, rather than providing a null as the RebalanceListener to the callbacks.
Good idea. Passing in a mock rebalanceConsumer and verified no interactions with it after each test.
nit: This does seem like an ideal opportunity to call it `TheRebalanceListener`.
Doesn't this call to `subscribe(_,_)` and the next one need to be updated too?
So, it turns out these invoke a `StreamsRebalanceListener` and not the regular `ConsumerRebalanceListener`. Should this API be updated as well as a follow-on? I deliberately left it  out of KIP-1306.
This is a good question. @lucasbru for awareness.
Let me file a JIRA for it so we can continue the discussion there?

It's an internal interface, so yeah it doesn't belong into the KIP.

We can make it consistent with the KIP, but it doesn't really belong into this PR.

Feel free to open a minor JIRA for it.

StreamsRebalanceListener goes unused. Pass a mock instead of null and verify no
interactions after each test.
